what_its_for: Cannabidiol is used to treat certain types of severe seizures in people with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, Dravet syndrome, or tuberous sclerosis complex. It belongs to a class of medicines called anticonvulsants and works by reducing abnormal electrical activity in the brain that causes seizures.
how_to_take: Take cannabidiol by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. It comes as an oral liquid solution. Use only the measuring device (oral syringe or dosing cup) that comes with your medicine to measure each dose carefully. You can take it with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. If you take it with food, always take it with food to keep your levels steady. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can make your seizures worse.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time. The dose is based on your weight and the condition being treated. A typical starting dose is 2.5 mg per kilogram of body weight taken twice daily (5 mg/kg/day total). Your doctor may increase your dose up to 10 mg/kg/day or even 20 mg/kg/day depending on how well it works and how you tolerate it. Always follow your doctor's specific dosing instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store the unopened bottle at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Once you open the bottle, you may store it at room temperature or in the refrigerator. Use the medicine within 12 weeks of first opening the bottle, then throw away any remaining medicine. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Store out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze. Do not use if the liquid looks unusual or if the expiration date has passed.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking cannabidiol, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and may raise the risk of liver problems. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL other medications you take, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements, because cannabidiol can interact with many medicines, especially other seizure medications like valproate and clobazam. Avoid taking more than the prescribed dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe nausea or vomiting, stomach pain, loss of appetite, or unusual tiredness — these could be signs of liver problems. Also call your doctor if you experience: thoughts of hurting yourself or suicide, new or worsening depression or anxiety, unusual mood or behavior changes, severe drowsiness or sleepiness, or if your seizures get worse or change in type. Tell your doctor if you become pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
when_it_works: You may not see the full benefit of cannabidiol right away. It may take several weeks to find the right dose and to see the most improvement in seizure control. Do not stop taking the medicine even if you do not notice changes right away. Keep all follow-up appointments so your doctor can check how the medicine is working and monitor for side effects, including regular blood tests to check your liver.
special_populations: Children: Cannabidiol is approved for use in children as young as 1 year old for certain seizure conditions, but dosing is carefully based on body weight. Older Adults: Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like drowsiness and dizziness. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The risks and benefits should be carefully discussed with your doctor. Liver Problems: If you have liver disease, your doctor may need to lower your dose or monitor you more closely. Valproate Users: If you also take valproate (valproic acid or divalproex), you are at a higher risk for liver problems and should be monitored closely.
